walkthroughs.h2: Why did Henry Tudor win at Bosworth?
walkthroughs.body_html: Richard III's seizure of the throne in 1483 and rumours of murdering his nephews alienated nobles. Henry Tudor landed at Milford Haven in August 1485 with French support. At Bosworth on 22 August the Stanleys delayed and then intervened against Richard; Richard was killed and Henry crowned on the field, ending decades of dynastic war.

walkthroughs.h2: How Henry VII tamed the nobility
walkthroughs.body_html: Henry restricted livery and maintenance, exploited bonds and recognisances to bind nobles financially, and used Acts of Attainder to confiscate land from opponents. The Council Learned in the Law under Empson and Dudley enforced royal rights aggressively. By 1509 the crown was solvent and the aristocracy more dependent on royal favour.

Henry pursued recognition and trade rather than glory. The Treaty of Medina del Campo (1489) arranged Catherine of Aragon's marriage to Arthur; the Treaty of Etaples (1492) bought off French support for Warbeck; the Magnus Intercursus (1496) secured Burgundian trade. By his death in 1509 Henry left a stable throne and full treasury.
